papers.title: Constructing 3D BN network in epoxy via magnetic field-assisted tape casting for enhanced thermal conduction performance
papers.abstract: Hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) has a layered structure that endows it high thermal conductivity along (00 l ) plane, making h-BN and boron nitride nanosheets (BNNS) ideal fillers for thermal interface materials. In this study, glycine modified BN (Gly-BN) and BNNS were prepared by ball-milling assisted ultrasonic liquid-phase exfoliation, and then magnetically modified Fe 3 O 4 @BNNS (F@B) was prepared by the in situ synthesis of Fe 3 O 4 on BNNS. The magnetic field-assisted tape casting method was employed to construct the three-dimensional (3D) BN network structure in epoxy with the mass ratio of BN in F@B to BN in Gly-BN fixed at 1:1 and the total BN content in the composite fixed at 30 wt%. Gly-BN was horizontally oriented under the action of the casting scraper and Fe 3 O 4 @BNNS was vertically oriented under magnetic field. When the mass ratio of Fe 3 O 4 to BNNS in F@B is 1:1 and the applied magnetic field strength is 60 mT, the in-plane thermal conductivity of Gly-BN/Fe 3 O 4 @BNNS/EP (G/F@B/E) composite reaches 4.86 W/(m·K), and its through-plane thermal conductivity is 1.84 W/(m·K). The material exhibits excellent heat dissipation performance when used as a thermal interface material (TIM) between an LED and a heat sink, demonstrating its great potential using as TIM in electronic devices.

papers.title: Hierarchically structured PVDF/Graphene Oxide-Nanodiamond nanofibrous membranes with enhanced wettability and Oil/Water separation
papers.abstract: Oil-in-water emulsion separation remains challenging because membranes must combine suitable wettability, high separation efficiency, and resistance to fouling. In this study, electrospun PVDF nanofibrous membranes incorporating graphene oxide-nanodiamond (GO-ND) nanohybrids were developed for oily wastewater treatment. The optimized membrane exhibited a hierarchical fibrous morphology and improved surface wettability, with the water contact angle decreasing from approximately 143° for pristine PVDF to 71°, while the underwater oil contact angle increased from 27° to 106°. Incorporation of 0.75 wt% GO–ND also improved the mechanical properties, increasing tensile strength from 4.27 to 7.81 MPa and elongation at break from 24.2% to 37.9%. Under gravity-driven filtration, the optimized membrane achieved fluxes of 367, 350, and 299 LMH, with oil rejection efficiencies of 96.11%, 97.12%, and 94.24% for hexane-, toluene-, and motor-oil-in-water emulsions, respectively. For surfactant-stabilized toluene emulsions, fluxes of 273.8 and 256 LMH were obtained with sodium dodecyl sulfate and Tween 80, respectively. After 20 filtration cycles, the membrane retained approximately 87.5% of its initial flux and 94% of its initial oil rejection. These results highlight the effectiveness of GO-ND nanohybrids in enhancing membrane wettability, mechanical robustness, and separation efficiency for oily wastewater treatment.

papers.title: Abrasive waterjet cutting of FFF-printed ASA/aramid composites: Effects of process parameters on kerf taper, surface roughness and edge damage
papers.abstract: Abrasive waterjet cutting of fibre-reinforced thermoplastics produced by fused filament fabrication (FFF) remains insufficiently understood, particularly for layered short-fibre composites. This study quantifies the effects of abrasive mass flow rate and traverse speed on kerf taper and jet-exit roughness in FFF-printed acrylonitrile styrene acrylate (ASA) containing 10 wt% aramid fibres, complemented by a qualitative assessment of visible cut-edge damage. A full-factorial design comprised 32 cuts, with abrasive mass flow rates of 50–400 g·min −1 and traverse speeds of 100–400 mm·min −1 at a constant pressure of 415 MPa and stand-off distance of 4 mm. Kerf geometry, contact profilometry and digital microscopy were used to assess cut quality. Both process factors significantly affected kerf taper and roughness parameters Ra and Rz. A nonlinear regression model described kerf taper (R 2 = 0.905), with traverse speed dominant and a significant quadratic effect of abrasive mass flow rate. Linear models described Ra and Rz (R 2 = 0.852 and 0.815), with abrasive mass flow rate dominant. Microscopy revealed local edge irregularities and material loss at the jet exit, with no pronounced interlayer separation visible at the observation scale used. These findings identify response-dependent process-parameter effects within the investigated range.

papers.title: Osteon topography-mimetic β-TCP/PCL membrane loaded with alendronate for the bidirectional regulation of guided bone regeneration
papers.abstract: Alveolar bone resorption, a hallmark of periodontitis, stems from an inflammation-induced imbalance in bone metabolism marked by excessive osteoclastogenesis and suppressed osteogenesis. Current guided bone regeneration (GBR) membranes lack bidirectional modulation, failing to achieve synergistic pro-osteogenic and anti-osteoclastogenic effects. Here, we engineered an alendronate-loaded osteon-mimetic β-TCP/PCL membrane (ALN@M-TCP/PCL) using soft lithography and melt-casting. This membrane integrates concentric microgrooves, uniformly dispersed β-tricalcium phosphate (β-TCP) particles, and an alendronate (ALN) coating. The membrane exhibited a biphasic, staged release of ALN and Ca 2+ characterized by an early burst followed by sustained delivery over 3–5 weeks. In vitro, it promoted osteogenesis in MC3T3-E1 monocultures while strongly inhibiting osteoclastogenesis. In an osteoblast–osteoclast co-culture model, the membrane reshaped paracrine crosstalk: the altered secretory factors suppressed osteoclast differentiation by lowering the RANKL/OPG ratio and reciprocally stimulating osteogenesis through elevated BMP-2 and oncostatin M (OSM). In vivo, ALN@M-TCP/PCL maximized new bone volume and osteocalcin (OCN) deposition while minimizing TRAP-positive osteoclast accumulation. By coupling biomimetic topography with targeted pharmacological cues, this membrane enables bidirectional intervention in bone metabolism, offering a promising strategy for alveolar bone regeneration in osteoclast-hyperactive microenvironments.

papers.title: Study on droplet impact, spreading and infiltration behavior, and granule binding mechanisms in binder jet 3D printing
papers.abstract: Binder jet 3D printing (BJ-3DP) offers unique advantages for fabricating personalized pharmaceutical formulations, but its process control is limited by insufficient understanding of droplet-powder interactions. In this study, a high-speed visualization platform was established to investigate droplet impact behavior on pharmaceutical powder beds. The effects of powder properties, powder-bed density, Weber number ( We ), and ink composition on impact dynamics and agglomerate formation were systematically evaluated. The results showed that powder characteristics and bed density jointly determined the interaction mode. A higher powder-bed density suppressed bed collapse, accelerated penetration, and promoted the formation of dense and uniform agglomerates. We was identified as an important parameter affecting spreading, penetration, and cratering, while viscous dissipation, wettability, solvent evaporation, and powder-bed resistance also contributed to the overall behavior. Low- We droplets favored stable spreading–penetration and uniform agglomeration, whereas high- We droplets induced splashing, prolonged penetration, and reduced deposition precision. Ink composition further regulated droplet behavior through surface tension, wettability, evaporation, and ink-powder compatibility. Overall, this study proposes a mechanism-based and semi-quantitative framework for understanding how local droplet-powder interactions may guide formulation design and process-window determination in pharmaceutical BJ-3DP.
